subject: Mutual action plan & billing path for Mira Health Azure private offer
messages:
From: Sara Dunne <sara.dunne@mirahealth.org>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Rivas <trivas@mirahealth.org>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Interest in Azure private offer + MAP request

Hi Soojin,

We're kicking off a short evaluation of Redwood for clinical triage at Mira Health. Legal/procurement are asking for a mutual action plan that ties the evaluation milestones to procurement steps and the billing path (we prefer Azure private offer if possible). Can you send a one-page MAP and confirm typical acceptance criteria, invoice timing, and what evidence you provide for SOC2/audit?

High level: 30-day pilot, then 3-month staging if pilot metrics look good. Procurement wants:
- PO timeline and invoice cadence
- Exact SKU/billing itemization for our FinOps team
- Any minimum commitment or cancel rules on private offers

Can Kimberly or you share an example MAP for an Azure private offer and a short checklist for our finance/legal?

Thanks — Sara
Sara Dunne
Sr. Procurement Manager, Mira Health
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Sara Dunne <sara.dunne@mirahealth.org>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interest in Azure private offer + MAP request

Hi Sara — thanks for the note and the clear asks. Attaching a concise MAP and a SOC2 summary for your review (see attachments). Below is a short cadence we typically run for Azure private-offer deals; we can compress timelines if you need.

Proposed MAP (high level):
- Week 0: NDA & pilot SOW signed (we can accept electronic PO to kick off).
- Week 1: Technical onboarding — access to sandbox + sample dataset ingestion.
- Week 2–3: Pilot run (30 days total) — weekly check-ins, success metrics collected (latency, accuracy, cost per 1k tokens).
- Week 5: Pilot readout & acceptance decision (go/no-go).
- Week 6–8: If go, transition to staging with provisioned private capacity via Azure private offer.
- Week 9: Production cutover + billing switch to private-offer invoice.

Billing path notes:
- Azure private offer (preferred): Redwood issues an invoice to Mira via Azure marketplace reconciliation flow. Invoice cadence can be monthly or quarterly depending on your AP needs; we typically do monthly for pilots and either monthly or net-30 for committed capacity.
- Alternative (hosted): Redwood invoices directly (useful if marketplace procurement blocks are long).

Required procurement artifacts:
- Example PO template (we've included a line-item SKU suggestion in the MAP attachment)
- SOC2 summary + relevant pen-test report (attached)
- Simple SOW for a 30-day pilot (we can draft)

I'll kick this to Kimberly for Azure private-offer legal/terms details and to Karthik for technical acceptance gates. If Tom (cc) has finance constraints, let us know cadence preferences.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Sara Dunne <sara.dunne@mirahealth.org>, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: trivas@mirahealth.org, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 13 Oct 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interest in Azure private offer + MAP request

Sara — looping in the legal/offer team. A few clarifications from procurement/legal side that will affect the private-offer doc:

1) Invoicing party: Azure private offer supports either marketplace-mediated invoice (Azure issues invoice to customer, Microsoft collects and transfers funds to Redwood) or vendor-billed with reconciliation through Azure. We prefer marketplace-mediated invoicing for customers who want unified cloud billing.

2) Minimum commitment: Private offers can be structured with committed capacity or as a consumption-only SKU. For pilots we recommend consumption-only to avoid commit negotiations. For reserved capacity we typically define commit tiers, discount levels, and an annual invoice schedule if requested.

3) Termination/cancel: For consumption pilots, customers can cancel without penalty at end of pilot. For committed tiers, standard contract language applies (pro-rated credits, early-termination fee depending on negotiated structure).

4) SKU detail: See attached MAP spreadsheet; I included a pilot SKU that maps to a monthly usage band (pilot expected spend: ~$8–12k/month based on your projected throughput). Please have your FinOps review the itemization with Tom.

I can produce a private-offer term sheet (Azure template) once we have the target invoice cadence and whether you'll accept marketplace invoicing. If Mira wants to try vendor invoicing first to shorten procurement path, we can support that for the pilot.

Kimberly Park
Senior Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_mpa_v1.xlsx
From: Tom Rivas <trivas@mirahealth.org>

Thanks — quick finance note:
- Prefer marketplace-mediated invoice on Azure to keep cloud spend consolidated.
- Monthly invoicing is OK for pilots; for any reserved commit we'll want quarterly invoicing and a standard net-30 payment window.
- Please include an account code field on line items so our chargeback system can map spend to clinical ops.

Sara, I'll draft a short PO once Redwood confirms SKU lines and the invoice party.
